text:
support-oncall: FYI customer AcmeDocs reporting a sudden spike of 5xx / timeouts hitting hosted inference around 11:20 UTC. They see lots of 504s and application timeouts. attaching logs and sample request. urgent. :rotating_light:

maria: on it, can you paste the tenant_id + a sample request body? any recent deploys?

support-oncall: tenant_id=acmedocs-prod-12, sample curl below. no deploys in the last 2h according to deploy-bot.

support-oncall: ```curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-beta","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":512}'``` 

kai: I pulled metrics for tenant acmedocs-prod-12. Request queue depth jumped from ~30 -> 120 around 11:18 UTC and continuous-batcher backlog increased sharply. p95 token latency climbed to 9s then 24s and started triggering gateway timeouts (504). Logs show dequeue stalls and long KV cache read tails.

infra-bot: automated alert: gateway_5xx_rate tenant=acmedocs-prod-12 rate=28% window=5m peak=42%

maria: can you post a snippet from request-queue logs (dequeue failures / timeout errors)? looking for messages like "batcher dequeue timed out" or "eviction dropped request"

support-oncall: pasted relevant lines below.

support-oncall: ```[11:19:21] request-queue: enqueue tenant=acmedocs-prod-12 id=... depth=92
[11:19:27] continuous-batcher: created batch id=bb-457 size=64 timeout_ms=12000
[11:19:39] request-queue: dequeue attempted id=... waited_ms=12800 -> timed out
[11:19:40] gateway: respond 504 tenant=acmedocs-prod-12 id=... reason=dequeue_timeout
[11:19:41] kvcache: read miss tenant=acmedocs-prod-12 key=tokcache shard=2 latency_ms=45
[11:19:47] continuous-batcher: batch id=bb-457 executing size=64 duration_ms=8400
[11:19:55] request-queue: enqueue tenant=acmedocs-prod-12 id=... depth=118
[11:19:59] gateway: 5xx surge: downstream 502/503/504 increasing
``` 

ashley: looks like tail latency from large batches is blocking the queue. many requests are short (few tokens) but are grouped into big batches because batching window is generous. that increases p99 and causes timeouts for subsequent dequeues.

kai: confirmed. workload skew: 60% short requests, 40% long-generation requests. continuous-batcher configured with max_batch_size=128 and max_wait_ms=12000. KV cache warmup also causing per-shard hotspots so some batches take >8s.

maria: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) reduce max_wait_ms to 50ms for this tenant or route to a low-latency policy 2) enforce per-tenant max_batch_size=16 3) route to model-variant with faster decoding (int8) 4) temporarily enable aggressive prefix caching or disable continuous-batcher for this tenant 5) raise gateway per-tenant concurrency limits to allow parallel small batches. which can we do quickly?

kai: I can patch routing policy to apply a tenancy override and reduce max_wait_ms + max_batch_size for acmedocs-prod-12. will do a quick canary on 1% then 20% then 100%. starting canary now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: route-override/acmedocs-batching-2026-03-17 by kai (canary 1%)

maria: also spinning up an extra dedicated inference pool (burst) to absorb backlog. provisioning GPU pool now, ETA ~4m.

infra-bot: metric snapshot: request_queue_depth (tenant=acmedocs-prod-12) before=118 now=84 after canary=68 p95_latency before=24000ms now=8200ms

support-oncall: after canary some 5xx decreased but still seeing tail timeouts at p99. customer reports partial recovery but intermittent 504s remain.

kai: bumping canary to 20%. also toggling continuous-batcher for short-request route to disabled so short jobs go through immediate-exec path.

deploy-bot: route update: canary=20% -> applied

ashley: important: disabling continuous-batcher for short path reduces throughput efficiency but improves latency. long-term we should tune batching heuristics (adaptive windowing) and add small-request fast lane.

maria: dedicated pool provisioned and attached to hosted cluster. extra workers accepted backlog, queue depth dropped to 22. gateway 5xx rate dropped from 28% -> 4% over 6m.

infra-bot: alert resolved: gateway_5xx_rate tenant=acmedocs-prod-12 cleared

support-oncall: customer confirming full recovery now. they saw retries succeed within seconds. :white_check_mark:

kai: follow-ups: 1) implement per-tenant fast-lane with strict batch caps 2) add queue depth circuit breaker to proactively fail/route before dequeue timeout 3) add tenant-level batching policy overrides in Console UI 4) postmortem and customer RCA

ashley: adding to backlog: adaptive batching heuristics, KV cache shard rebalancer, and enhanced per-tenant observability (queue depth heatmap).

maria: opening incident ticket and scheduling postmortem doc. will include timeline, metrics, logs, mitigation steps, and customer comms draft.

support-oncall: customer follow-up: "Thanks, recovered — please keep us posted on root cause & mitigation plan."

maria: noted. assigning P0 incident owner and scheduling 30m postmortem at 14:00 UTC. attaching this thread to the incident.

kai: final note: reproduction steps for eng if needed: send mixed workload with 60% short (10 tokens) and 40% long (600 tokens) at QPS=80 for tenant override header x-tenant=acmedocs-prod-12; observe queue depth and batch sizes. sample load test script:

kai: ```# simple k6-style pseudo
for i in 1..80 do
  if rand() < 0.6 then payload = {input: "short"} else payload = {input: "long..." * 200}
  http.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", json=payload, headers={"Authorization":"Bearer xxx","X-Tenant":"acmedocs-prod-12"})
end``` 

ashley: logging note: add counters for per-batch-execution-duration and per-batch-kvcache-miss to help debug future tail events.

maria: thanks everyone. keeping thread open for postmortem notes. :memo:
